ai_policy_disclosure.stage_1: Independent Diagnosis: Review the AI-generated engineering artifact directly. Do not paste external LLM fixes.
ai_policy_disclosure.stage_2: Independent Architectural Reasoning: Solve the baseline design and requirement pivot using your own engineering judgment.
ai_policy_disclosure.stage_3: Live Ownership Defense: Defend your Stage 1 and Stage 2 choices with concise, evidence-grounded reasoning.

rubric_bands.0: Fails to locate core algorithmic, validation, or concurrency bugs or proposes changes that break correctness.
rubric_bands.25: Names surface syntax issues without identifying runtime complexity, DB contention, or silent failure mechanisms.
rubric_bands.50: Locates 2 of 4 defects accurately but misses concurrency/complexity root cause or leaves subtle regression in patch.
rubric_bands.75: Locates >=3 of 4 defects with accurate causal explanation and supplies structurally sound AST-verified fix.
rubric_bands.100: Locates all defects precisely, explains worst-case runtime/DB mechanics, and produces clean, defensive fix.

rubric_bands.0: Proposes incompatible components or ignores Stage 2 constraints and Part B requirement shift.
rubric_bands.25: Lists generic stack buzzwords (Kafka/Redis/microservices) without linking them to bottleneck or SLA.
rubric_bands.50: Solves Part A reasonably but fails to adapt schema/caching/rollback coherently under Part B twist.
rubric_bands.75: Selects cohesive API, DB indexing/transaction, and scaling primitives and adapts clearly to Part B twist with >=1 explicit trade-off.
rubric_bands.100: Demonstrates end-to-end bottleneck analysis, quantifies consistency/cost trade-offs, and designs clean zero-downtime/canary mitigation.

rubric_bands.0: Proposes no test verification or tests only happy-path inputs.
rubric_bands.25: Mentions 'write unit tests' generically without specifying inputs, assertions, or failure cases.
rubric_bands.50: Identifies 1-2 basic boundary cases (e.g. empty list) but misses concurrency, timeout, or integration boundaries.
rubric_bands.75: Specifies concrete unit + integration test cases covering null/empty inputs, invalid payloads, and duplicate/error paths.
rubric_bands.100: Designs comprehensive pytest/integration matrix isolating deterministic logic, race/retry idempotency, and CI/CD regression gates.

rubric_bands.0: Accepts flawed AI code/assumptions as production-ready without skepticism.
rubric_bands.25: Critiques formatting/comments rather than hidden correctness, security, or performance flaws.
rubric_bands.50: Questions AI snippet superficially without identifying why the AI pattern fails under production data or load.
rubric_bands.75: Pinpoints misleading AI assumptions (e.g. hidden O(N^2), swallowed exceptions, unsafe concurrency) and explains verification checks.
rubric_bands.100: Systematically separates valid AI scaffolding from subtle failure modes and defines repeatable review guardrails.

rubric_bands.0: Evades Stage 3 follow-up questions, contradicts prior answers, or refuses to address failure modes.
rubric_bands.25: Repeats prior statements verbatim without engaging the interviewer's constraint or counter-example.
rubric_bands.50: Responds to challenge defensively or partially updates design without tracing downstream impact.
rubric_bands.75: Engages follow-ups directly with Stage 1-2 evidence, acknowledges oversight cleanly if shown a bug, and states operational impact.
rubric_bands.100: Demonstrates high-agency ownership: defends valid trade-offs under pressure, revises weak spots decisively, and covers monitoring/rollback.

stage_1.prompt: An AI coding assistant drafted this Python service helper to deduplicate incoming order batches and decrement cached/DB stock. Review the artifact, localize all 4 defects, submit a safe Python patch, and list concrete pytest cases.

planted_defects.label: O(N^2) linear scan over processed orders and catalog_items inside nested loop
Missing validation for None inputs, negative/zero qty, or missing dict keys
Bare Exception swallowed with pass hides DB/stock failures silently
Check-then-act stock check on stale in-memory item dict risks overselling under concurrent requests

ast_invariants.description: Must not swallow exceptions silently with except ...: pass
Must include explicit input/quantity validation guard
Deduplicate using set/dict index rather than O(N^2) any(...) scan

part_a.title: Flash-Sale Checkout API Design
part_a.prompt: You are building the REST API & PostgreSQL checkout pipeline behind `process_order_batch` for 50 req/sec steady traffic. Specify your DB transaction/locking choice, API idempotency contract, and deployment strategy.

part_b_twist.title: Requirement Pivot: 10x Flash Spike & Duplicate Webhooks
part_b_twist.prompt: Constraint Shift: Flash-sale traffic jumps to 500 req/sec, p95 checkout latency must stay <= 100ms, and the payment gateway now retries webhooks up to 4 times out of order. Update your architecture without overselling inventory.

expected_adaptation_signals: Uses atomic conditional UPDATE or select_for_update / Redis atomic reservation + DB reconciliation
Enforces unique idempotency key constraint for webhook retries
Defines p95 latency / lock-contention alerts and canary/rollback switch

twist_pool: What happens in your Stage 2 solution if Redis reservation succeeds but PostgreSQL commit times out 100ms later?
Your Stage 1 fix still mutates catalog_items in memory or skips concurrency test cases — design one deterministic test proving zero double-deduction.

task_bundles.title: Tenant Export Worker & Query Pipeline Review

stage_1.prompt: An AI assistant generated this Python background worker function to compile per-tenant CSV billing summaries from ORM repositories. Identify all 4 defects, submit a safe structural Python fix, and specify test cases.

planted_defects.label: N+1 repository queries per tenant inside loop instead of batched/aggregated query
Missing None check when db.get_tenant(tid) or inv['amount'] is missing/null
Accumulates unbounded in-memory all_rows list without chunking/streaming pagination
Uses integer/float zero sum on financial amounts without Decimal/currency validation or empty guard

ast_invariants.description: Must guard missing tenant/None or invalid tenant_ids input
Avoid unbounded per-tenant N+1 loop accumulation without batching/yield

part_a.title: Async Export API & PostgreSQL Indexing
part_a.prompt: Design the API and worker pipeline allowing enterprise tenants with 200k invoices to trigger CSV exports cleanly without blocking web Gunicorn workers.

part_b_twist.title: Requirement Pivot: Poison-Pill Tenant & 15s Freshness SLA
part_b_twist.prompt: Constraint Shift: Corrupted UTF-16 invoice rows from one tenant crash shared worker retries repeatedly, while small tenants demand <15s export turnaround during billing close.

expected_adaptation_signals: Separates fast-lane small exports from large queued exports (priority queues/streaming)
Isolates poison-pill payloads via dead-letter queue + per-row validation error reporting
Adds PostgreSQL composite index (tenant_id, created_at) and worker memory/failure metrics

twist_pool: If a worker dies halfway through writing a 200k-row export to S3/Cloudinary, how do you prevent partial corrupted downloads?
Walk through an integration test that catches both N+1 query regression and a null tenant record.

task_bundles.title: API Token Auth & Rate-Limiter Middleware Review

stage_1.prompt: An AI assistant generated this Python request guard handling bearer token verification and per-user rate limiting. Diagnose all 4 defects, patch the logic structurally, and write critical security/edge tests.

planted_defects.label: except Exception returns True (fail-open bypasses all authentication on cache/store error)
Ignores now_ts token expiration check and uses non-constant-time == comparison
Naive .replace('Bearer ', '') accepts empty/missing scheme or case/whitespace bypasses
Non-atomic read-then-write rate counter allows concurrent burst bypass and never expires window

ast_invariants.description: Exception handlers in auth logic must never return True
Must validate Bearer scheme, token emptiness, and expiry against now_ts

part_a.title: Multi-Worker Auth & Rate Limiting Architecture
part_a.prompt: Deploy this auth/rate-limiting layer across 8 Gunicorn web workers behind Nginx with PostgreSQL token revocation support.

part_b_twist.title: Requirement Pivot: Cache Store Outage & Latency Budget
part_b_twist.prompt: Constraint Shift: Shared Redis rate-limit cache experiences a 3-minute partition while external SSO validation spikes to 2.5s. Keep unauthorized access strictly zero while preserving legitimate traffic.

expected_adaptation_signals: Fails closed for authentication while applying bounded circuit-breaker/local fallback for rate limiting
Never trusts per-worker LocMemCache as authoritative revocation state
Monitors 401/429/503 surges and defines short-lived signed token vs. revocation list trade-off

twist_pool: Explain the trade-off between failing open vs. failing closed on rate limiting versus authentication during a cache outage.
Write assertions for a test suite verifying expired tokens, malformed headers, and simulated store exceptions.
